content: The United Nations International Drug Control Programme (UNDCP) and the United Nations Centre for International Crime Prevention (CICP) are integral components of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), which was previously known as the United Nations Office for Drug Control and Crime Prevention (ODCCP). The UNDCP collaborates with various governmental and non-governmental organizations, as well as the private sector, to address drug control issues. Currently, it is formulating plans to enhance its engagement with the private sector through a more focused and strategic approach. A team of experts within the UNDCP assists states that request support in becoming parties to and implementing the United Nations drug control conventions. Additionally, the UNDCP provides laboratory services, develops training materials, and refers individuals in need to appropriate medical advice. In central, eastern, and southeastern Europe, the UNDCP has concentrated its efforts on fostering cross-border cooperation by harmonizing national drug control capacities. A significant aspect of its work in this region has been the establishment of a coordination mechanism to facilitate international drug control assistance for Eastern Europe, the Baltic States, and the Commonwealth of Independent States. An external evaluation has confirmed the necessity of coordinating technical assistance projects in the foreseeable future due to the complexity of recipient countries' needs and the involvement of multiple donors in the target regions. The UNDCP's coordination mechanism has played a pivotal role in aligning strategies for collaboration among donor countries and international organizations in the field of drug control. This coordination framework is increasingly being utilized to develop joint strategies between the UNDCP and donors, as well as to design and implement technical cooperation projects and programs. Efforts to further develop this mechanism were ongoing during the years 2000–2001. In the area of demand reduction, a multi-phase regional program aimed at training professionals in the treatment of drug abuse has been successfully completed. This initiative has resulted in the creation of a core group of over 600 trained professionals and the establishment of sustainable national training programs. The UNDCP has also continued its collaboration with the Pompidou Group of the Council of Europe to expand its city network to include states in Eastern Europe. It has worked with the International Labour Organization (ILO) to implement a UNDCP-funded workplace prevention program and partnered with the Associazione Casa Famiglia Rosetta to train professionals in the treatment of drug abuse.
